utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Maric, have you ever seen any kind of document that would indicate that the Convicts' Battalion was under the command of the Main Staff of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I just said something about it. No, I have never seen such a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In view of your knowledge of the situation on the ground throughout this period, was Mr. Milivoj Petkovic able to issue orders to Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, an order that the latter would obey?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at P1866. It's minutes of a meeting in the operation zone south-east Herzegovina of 30th April. It will be easier now, Mr. Maric, if you open the file in front of you.

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Just let me tell you how the documents are organised. If you open the file, the first documents in line will be Prosecution documents, and this one is P1866. I'm being told that it's the first one. That is the document you discussed with my learned friend Mrs. West. This document says -- and you remember what my colleague Ms. West asked you. The document says: "Reports have been read from the areas of Konjic and Jablanica that had arrived in the operation zone over the last two days." And after that certain conclusions were adopted. Let's now look at 1784 [as interpreted] to see what kind of reports were discussed. It's P1874. This is a summary report for the date of 13th April. And on page 2, item 3, is a report from your operation zone. I will just give in bullet points the key events. The Croat village of Buscak was attacked with all types of infantry weapons and 120-millimetre mortars. Around 50 shells were fired. Buturovic Polje was targeted with about 15 shells, and the shelling of Kostajnica is ongoing, and attacks are starting in Konjic which is under siege as is Jablanica. Then there is a second report from Konjic on the same day. Buscak village is about to fall, and then Buscak has fallen. We are fearing a massacre. Please send the Red Cross. And then it says: Urgently act upon our previous request addressed to Prozor. It's in fact a request for artillery fire on designated targets. And the next report says again that there is fierce fire from mortars on Ljesovina, Buturovic Polje, and Kostajnica. Conclusion: This is an all-out attack on the entire zone of Konjic and Jablanica. To the best of your recollection, Mr. Maric, is it true that on the 13th of April the situation was as described in this report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In para 3 of the document shown to you by my colleague Ms. West, it says that tasks need to be determined especially by the staff in case of clash with the Muslims. Do you interpret this -- do you read this as preparations for attack or for defence?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Ms. West quoted a part of your summary and asked you to comment on the passage where it says that certain documents can be understood properly only if you are familiar with the developments in the broader area. Do I need to refresh your memory on this?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is P1928. This is an order from the commander of the 1st Brigade of HVO Nedjeljko Obradovic, dated 17 April 1993. And in paragraph 1 of this order it says that from the existing battalions of the 1st Brigade, one separate unit needs to be formed, composed of Croats only. In para 5 it reads: "I hold commanders of the battalions answerable for the implementation of the task." Tell us, this term "task," is it in the plural or in the singular? In para 5.

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "commanders" individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No, I meant to ask: Is it one task, in the singular, is it clear?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see now what this task could be. Let's look at document 4D1715. This is a special report from the security department of the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces, where it says - and I will try to summarise briefly - it's the fourth paragraph. In Croatian, it's page 2. It says that on the 18th of April, 1993, that is, a day after this order was issued, a hundred HVO members took up positions. And the next day, 19 April, around 15 HVO members arrived at Gubavica. And then there followed an HVO attack, and the command of the HVO entered the barracks and informed members of the Bregava Brigade that they had militarily occupied the barracks in the area of Gubavica. And then in paragraph 6 of this document, it says that on the 22nd of April the HVO attacked the command which with the brigade police was breaking through in the direction of Stolac, where they were ambushed near Osanice in which incident all 20 of them were captured and taken to a camp along with Bregava Brigade members captured earlier. If you look at these documents, do they give you any reason to associate this special report of the security section with the assignment, the task, given by Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us about the Bregava Brigade of the Bosnian army. Was it in your area of responsibility of the operations zone?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in our area of responsibility, and it was under the command of the military district commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is 4D473, and this is a document that the Bregava Brigade commander of the BH army sent to the 1st Brigade commander of the HVO on the 18th of April, 1993. It's just one in a series of documents that form their correspondence. I had -- I have shown some earlier in our case, but I'll limit myself to the passage on the second page. Bajro Pizovic says to Nedjeljko Obradovic, I quote: "I note, and you are aware of this perfectly well, that a large number of Muslim soldiers are part of your unit, but they are Muslims and they belong to this people, and it would not be good to disrupt a certain organisation and the formation of your units." If you had received a letter like this from a brigade commander of the BH army, how would you understand it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that the commander of this brigade was very well informed about the structure of personnel in another unit, and I would understand this as a certain dose of threat.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you as a military commander in such circumstances were trying to carry out an operation against the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would you try for your unit to be made up of ethnic Croat soldiers predominantly or exclusively for that matter?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If one were to embark on a serious operation against the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it would be advisable for it to consist of mostly Croats in order to prevent any trouble.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Next document, 4D36, please. This is a report of the commander of the 4th Corps of the BH army to his superior command. I will present the content of this very briefly. In paragraph 3 it says, inter alia, that we've linked up with our people in the HVO. And then it says the personnel of the HVO from Capljina have the task of taking Tasovcici and the bridge in Capljina. And it says taking the town of Stolac with our people. Tell us, Mr. Maric, as a soldier what would your estimate be? Is the BH army counting on co-operation with the Muslim soldiers of the HVO or not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and these were the most difficult moments that could happen to a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To the best of your understanding, do these documents show that a document can be understood fully only if one knows of broader developments in the area?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document P1998 [as interpreted]. This is an order of the commander of the operative zone of the 20th of April, 1993, ordering the highest level of combat-readiness. If I understood this correctly, this was shown to you as a sort of preparatory order for the conflict that occurred in Mostar on the 9th of May. P1978, P1978. This is an order of Midhat Hujdur dated the 19th of April, 1993. The first question, Mr. Maric, have you ever heard of Midhat Hujdur?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him and planned with him and fought together with him against the Army of Republika Srpska in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us see what is being planned here. For the 1st Battalion it says -- I'm going to omit certain elements, and I'm going to refer to what I think is most important. The Mostar Brigade, once conditions are created, start attack at the crossroads of Mostar-Buna and Mostar-Blagaj, Mostar-Buna and Mostar-Blagaj. In further combat activity, try to link-up with the Blagaj independent company in the area of the Buna village, and part of the forces should be sent to the right bank of the Neretva and placed under the command of the commander of the 2nd Battalion. Furthermore, the lines that the 2nd Battalion is supposed to take are referred to, and it is ordered, inter alia, to block HVO forces in the rear of that line and carry out its neutralisation. Part of the forces from the 4th Company should be sent towards the command of the 41st Motorised Brigade to reinforce defence. My question, first of all, Mr. Maric, could you as a soldier tell us, when we say "neutralise HVO forces," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neutralisation means to operate temporarily at these forces in order to prevent them from carrying out the activity they had been carrying out until then involving the -- a certain level of destruction of those forces too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Now the 19th of April, what is the Mostar Brigade of the BH army planning? What is defined for the 3rd Battalion is in paragraph 1.3. It says: Close the axis from Vrapcic towards Mostar in the Sutina sector and make it impossible to cross the Mostar dam and also fully block -- and fully block and take the north camp barracks. Then the tasks of other units of the Ministry of the Interior are referred to, inter alia, in 1.8 it says that an attack should be carried out at the premises of the MUP of the HZ HB, and so on. Tell us, Mr. Maric, now these axes of activity and localities, do they mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, all of these locations are 2, 3, and even 7 kilometres behind the only lines where HVO units were at the time, and those were the lines facing the Army of Republika Srpska. That means that taking up strategic positions and taking strategic facilities in the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Another document in this context, 2D478, again Midhat Hujdur. The order is of the 20th of April, the next day, that is. What is ordered here is readiness to engage targets, and I'll tell you which ones: In the area of Cekrk, in the area of Nova Banka and the high school, in the area of Avenija Rudnik, and then Bijeli Brijeg, Rondo and the faculties, and some other locations are mentioned in paragraph 2. Tell me, the activity of the BH army on the 9th of May, 1993, did it have anything to do with these locations?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order, an order that was used by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it shows exactly how an attack operation is to be carried out with a view to breaking through and taking territories that are held by the unit that is attacked. So this fully corresponds to what happened on the morning of the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, in your view, do these documents confirm or deny the thesis that in order to understand documents properly one has to be familiar with broader developments on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document that I'd like to hear your brief comment on is D1125 -- P1125 [as interpreted], that is. 2215. [In English] P2215. [Interpretation] That is the order of Nedjeljko Obradovic of the 7th of May, 1993. It was discussed extensively. This order mentions IZM Stolac. Mr. Maric, do you know who the commander of the IZM of the HVO in Stolac was?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic was our witness, and we talked to him about this document as well. I would like to put the following question to you. To the best of your knowledge, the 1st Brigade of the HVO, did it take part in any way in the fighting that took place in Mostar on the 9th and 10th of April -- of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall any moment when the 1st Brigade took part in fighting in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Since we discussed part of this order that has to do with training in built-up areas, tell us about the towns of Stolac and Capljina, are they in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document, P2209. It is an order that bears the name of Milivoj Petkovic, head of the Main Staff. Please look at this order, Mr. Maric, and can you tell us who signed it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who signed it. It certainly wasn't General Petkovic. I have no idea who this is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Try to read the name. If I tell you Ivica, would you read the name Ivica in that signature? Very well. If you cannot --

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We're going to have a witness who will be in a position to talk about this. 3D 793 would be the next document, please. This is a document that contains the conclusions of a meeting of HVO commanders. Many questions were put in this regard by the Trial Chamber, and Ms. West asked you whether General Petkovic attended the meeting. You said that you are almost certain that he was not present at the meeting. So let us deal with this and let us do away with any dilemma, although General Praljak talked about it. Let us look at document P6491, please. It is in English and the document is dated the 7th of November, 1993. It's an UNPROFOR document and it says that the commander of the UNPROFOR forces for Bosnia-Herzegovina on that day met up with General Petkovic. Mr. Maric, I can just ask you once again, if you give this some careful thought, have you seen General Petkovic -- had you seen him at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General Petkovic did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now please look at document P6534. 6534. This is an order to attack. That is what is most important for us in these proceedings, the selective shelling of the town of Mostar. We see that it bears the name of General Petkovic. We do not see any signature. We've already said this in this courtroom. When I reacted to my colleague's question, I said that if we already have a statement to the effect that General Petkovic was not in Citluk on that day, we have to be very careful about that. Is it Petkovic's order, or does it just bear his name? Now I'd like to show you 4D8334, 4D834, 4D834. This is a document that was sent to Kiseljak to Mr. Rajic, to report as soon as possible on what happened in Stupni Do, to report to the Main Staff about that. The order -- or, rather, the letter was not signed by Mr. Petkovic, General Petkovic. On the basis of what General Praljak said, it was done by General Praljak himself because Petkovic was not in Citluk on that day. Tell us now, Mr. Maric, as a soldier if one wants to know exactly who the author of a particular order is, is it important to establish that said person is truly the author of that document or that he took part in the creation of that document?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is important to ascertain that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my re-direct is completed. I would like to thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Maric.

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Maric, the Trial Chamber thanks you for coming to testify for the Defence of General Petkovic. We wish you a safe return home, and I'm going to ask our usher to please escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It was very pleasant to be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For technical reasons we will break for 25 minutes, since the next witness will have -- will enjoy a number of protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours. [In English] Maybe I would ask for a private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm most grateful and good morning. It's a very brief matter, and it arises out of Exhibit Number 4D00618 that was referred to in re-examination by my learned friend, Ms. Alaburic. Mr. President, as you are aware, that exhibit number has another exhibit number, P11123, which was submitted by the Prosecution arising out of the testimony of Filipovic. There's no decision at the moment as to the admissibility of that particular document. Now, the Defence for Bruno Stojic has some disquiet, as on the face of the documents there is a clear disparity between the B/C/S, the Croatian original, and the English translation. This has been the subject of correspondence with the Office of the Prosecution, and it resulted in a filing of the 14th of December, 2009, in which my learned friend Mr. Scott very kindly at paragraph 3 went some way to allaying some of the concerns of the Defence when he acknowledged that the B/C/S version shows a line which is not on the English version, and they said that it might be considered that the B/C/S version of the document is more authoritative. It may be -- it might be considered -- it's not really clear enough in a criminal trial, it's not good enough from the Defence perspective to have a clear disparity of this nature. It is of course important because the line that's missing bypasses the defence department. It shows a clear direct relationship between the supreme commander and the Main Staff. Your Honours, I do ask the Court give consideration to ordering either - and, in fact, in fairness it should be both - the Defence for General Petkovic and also the Prosecution to re-file the translation so that it accords to what is the original. And so, Your Honours, I do ask that an order be made to the Prosecution in relation to Exhibit P11123 and the Defence for Petkovic arising out of 4D00618 to ensure that the translation of the document accords to the B/C/S original. Your Honours, I think that would make sure that there's absolute clarity and no misunderstanding at all, and, Your Honour, that is my application. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me consult with my fellow Judges.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... I just want to say, we are really now spending more time on this issue which is not a good idea. I just wish to say for the Petkovic Defence, it's important that the current document looked exactly the way General Petkovic used it in Blaskic, and we are prepared and willing to prepare a new schematic with correctly indicated lines in the English version and that would then be treated as a correction to the English translation. We wish you to know that General Petkovic testified precisely like that in those terms ten years ago and nothing has changed to this day. If you allow us, we will do that without delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether I understood you correctly. Are you saying that both these documents must be regarded as originals because both were used in this disparate way in the Blaskic trial?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both my colleagues in other Defences and we simply borrowed this schematic from the Blaskic case, which was admitted there. That was the point of the Stojic Defence. We cannot intervene in a document we are showing to you as a document from the Blaskic case, but we recognise the error in the English version and we are prepared to make the same schematic with the correct translation as a new document. And then you will know that the English version of this document is correct. We really think it's important to show you the document as it was in Blaskic; however, we cannot tender a document from another case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm afraid you have not answered my question, which is a very simple one. In Blaskic were they -- were there these two documents, B/C/S and English, with the same disparity? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. The Croatian text is correct, accurate. The Croatian is not the problem. It's the translation that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, I think I'm understanding it perhaps and understanding where the confusion is. If there was a discrepancy in the Blaskic case, which is what I'm understanding between the B/C/S and the English versions, then it looks as if what ought to happen is that the B/C/S version and the English version should have different exhibit numbers in this case. Because otherwise if they retain the same exhibit number, it rather implies that the English matches the B/C/S. So it looks as if in order to be very clear which document is which, they probably ought to be separately identified, but of course I support everything and agree with everything Ms. Alaburic has said. But that may be the practical correct technical solution.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we can just forestall any decision on this until after the break. I didn't realise this document was going to be used, and the Prosecution will just talk to Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session. The next hearing will be held on Monday at 1415. I wish everyone a nice afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
